acknowledgments.summary: Fortinet is pleased to thank Juan A. Zavala from EchoStar/HUGHES for reporting this vulnerability under responsible disclosure

notes.title: Summary
notes.text: An Improper Authentication vulnerability in the FortiOS Remote Radius Type Admin Two-Factor authentication

notes.title: Additional info
notes.text:
Workaround
Remove the Remote Radius Type Admin account linked to the RADIUS server that responds with an additional "Access-Challenge" message when the user fails to enter a valid two-factor authentication token.

In the GUI: 
Navigate to System > Administrators and delete the Remote Radius Type administrator accounts.

In the CLI:  
config system admin
delete < Remote type administrator account >
next
end

remediations.details:
FortiOS 8.0: Not Applicable
FortiOS 7.6: Upgrade to 7.6.7 or above
FortiOS 7.4: Not Applicable
FortiOS 7.2: Not Applicable

references.summary: An Improper Authentication vulnerability [CWE-287] in the FortiOS Remote Radius Type Admin Two-Factor (TFA) Authentication may allow a remote authenticated attacker with at least read-only permission to log in to the FortiOS GUI with an invalid token after entering a valid username and password, in scenarios where the  RADIUS server returns an additional "Access-Challenge" response following an invalid TFA token.
